entries.title: Song of Solomon 6:1
segments: Whither is thy beloved gone, O thou fairest among women? Whither hath thy beloved turned him, That we may seek him with thee?

entries.title: Song of Solomon 6:2
segments: My beloved is gone down to his garden, To the beds of spices, To feed in the gardens, and to gather lilies.

entries.title: Song of Solomon 6:3
segments: I am my beloved's, and my beloved is mine; He feedeth [his flock] among the lilies,

entries.title: Song of Solomon 6:4
segments: Thou art fair, O my love, as Tirzah, Comely as Jerusalem, Terrible as an army with banners.

entries.title: Song of Solomon 6:5
segments: Turn away thine eyes from me, For they have overcome me. Thy hair is as a flock of goats, That lie along the side of Gilead.

entries.title: Song of Solomon 6:6
segments: Thy teeth are like a flock of ewes, Which are come up from the washing; Whereof every one hath twins, And none is bereaved among them.

entries.title: Song of Solomon 6:7
segments: Thy temples are like a piece of a pomegranate Behind thy veil.

entries.title: Song of Solomon 6:8
segments: There are threescore queens, and fourscore concubines, And virgins without number.

entries.title: Song of Solomon 6:9
segments: My dove, my undefiled, is [but] one; She is the only one of her mother; She is the choice one of her that bare her. The daughters saw her, and called her blessed; [Yea], the queens and the concubines, and they praised her.

entries.title: Song of Solomon 6:10
segments: Who is she that looketh forth as the morning, Fair as the moon, Clear as the sun, Terrible as an army with banners?

entries.title: Song of Solomon 6:11
segments: I went down into the garden of nuts, To see the green plants of the valley, To see whether the vine budded, [And] the pomegranates were in flower.

entries.title: Song of Solomon 6:12
segments: Before I was aware, my soul set me [Among] the chariots of my princely people.

entries.title: Song of Solomon 6:13
segments: Return, return, O Shulammite; Return, return, that we may look upon thee. Why will ye look upon the Shulammite, As upon the dance of Mahanaim?
